title: Occupational Impact and Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathies (CIPN)
official: Occupational Impact and Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathies (CIPN): A Descriptive Study of Occupational Issues to Guide Occupational Therapy Intervention
summary:
Advances in cancer treatment have increased the number of patients living with long-term treatment-related consequences. Among these, chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is common and can significantly affect patients' quality of life and daily activities. Despite its impact, CIPN remains difficult to manage, and patients often receive insufficient support regarding its functional and occupational consequences.

Occupational therapy remains underutilised in oncology, despite its potential to help patients maintain or regain independence in meaningful daily activities. Collaboration between Advanced Practice Nurses and occupational therapists could improve the identification and management of occupational difficulties associated with CIPN.

The aim of this study is to describe the occupations affected by CIPN using the Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (COPM). The findings will help identify patients' occupational needs and guide future occupational therapy interventions.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patient treated for breast cancer or colorectal cancer, who has not previously received paclitaxel or oxaliplatin.
* Patient with grade 2 or 3 peripheral neuropathy, according to the CTCAE criteria, occurring during their treatment.
* Patient able to communicate in French.
* Patient aged 18 years or older

Exclusion Criteria:

* History of neuropathy prior to treatment.
* Refusal to participate in the study.
* Protected persons (pregnant or breastfeeding women, individuals under guardianship or curatorship, minors, individuals deprived of their liberty, or individuals unable to provide informed consent).
